details: CONFIRMED by reading: wait_pid has no notion of the writer being gone; at these two sites the read happens after
run_check returned, i.e. after bin/check has already killed the step, so nothing can write the file any more. The
analysis (row B, H2) accepted turning ValueError into the named failure, so this is not a regression of the promise,
but the 60 s is pure waiting and the residual flake stays (rate not measured; the analysis calls it rarer than H1).
evidence: tests/test_bin_check_portable.py:111-114 and 136-146 (read after run_check); tests/pidfile.py:20-33 (loop ends only on a
failing_case: test_hung_step_is_gone_afterwards (and test_perl_hang_is_hung_and_does_not_wait_extra, line 146) on a loaded machine where
the step `sh -c 'echo $$ > step.pid; exec sleep 30'` has not written its pid when bin/check's 1 s limit kills it: the file
is missing or empty and its writer is dead. Now: wait_pid polls for 60 s, then AssertionError "held no whole number
within 60 s: missing" (before: ValueError or FileNotFoundError at once). The test is still red in that case, and 60 s
later. Expected: either the case cannot arise (the step's pid is known before the limit can fire), or the test fails at
once with a message saying the step never wrote its pid.
fix_hint: Give wait_pid an optional `writer_alive: Callable[[], bool]` and fail at once with the file's text when it returns False;
these two sites pass `lambda: False` (the writer is already gone, so one read decides). The same parameter fixes F2.
pass_cases: - step writes its pid, bin/check kills it at 1 s: wait_pid returns the pid at once, the pid is not alive, test passes (as today).
- pid file missing after run_check returned (writer dead): the test ends within 1 s with a message naming "never wrote its pid", not after 60 s.
- perl variant: same two cases; the `took < 5` assertion still measures only run_check, not the pid wait.
reason: tests/test_pidfile.py WaitPid::test_a_dead_writer_that_left_nothing_fails_at_once_naming_it (and the wrote-before-dying and slow-live-writer cases) pass; bin-check sites pass writer_alive=lambda: False (test_bin_check_portable.py).
findings.summary: after bin/check has killed the step, wait_pid waits 60 s for a pid no live process can still write, then fails

details: CONFIRMED by reading the removed loop (`... and gate.poll() is None`) against wait_pid, which has no early stop. Only the
failure path changes (time and wording), so LOW. Size: 5 agent minutes once F1's parameter exists.
evidence: git diff master...HEAD -- tests/test_gate.py: the removed `while not os.path.exists(pid_file) and ... and gate.poll() is None`
failing_case: LeakedGates.start_orphan with a gate that exits at once (a broken repo setup, a gate refusing to start): before, the loop
stopped as soon as gate.poll() was not None and the test failed with "the gate command did not start"; now
wait_pid(pid_file, 60) waits the full 60 s and fails with "pid file ... held no whole number within 60 s: missing".
fix_hint: wait_pid(pid_file, 60, writer_alive=lambda: gate.poll() is None), with the parameter from F1.
pass_cases: - gate starts and its command writes the pid: start_orphan returns (gate, pid) as today.
- gate process exits before the pid file is written: start_orphan fails within about 1 s, naming that the gate ended before its command started.
- gate slow to start (pid written after 2 s, gate still running): start_orphan still waits and returns the pid.
reason: tests/test_gate.py start_orphan passes writer_alive=lambda: gate.poll() is None; behaviour covered by the WaitPid tests.
findings.summary: start_orphan no longer stops waiting when the gate exits before its command starts: 60 s wait and a vaguer message

details: CONFIRMED by reading line 143 (`[1]` drops the exit code). In practice a tip that does not exist fails here first, so
the new rev-list check is reached only when diff works and rev-list then fails (a timeout); the more likely git failure
is the one still answered as "not added". The outcome is a wrong closer (more often a spurious refusal than a wrong
pass), so LOW. Size: 5 agent minutes.
evidence: plugins/core/hooks/merge.py:143 `added = relay_git.git(main, "diff", ...)[1]`; the new test mocks this call as succeeding.
failing_case: closing_ref with ab = {"wt/a": <tip>} where `git diff --name-only ... master...<tip>` fails or passes relay_git's 20 s
limit (returns (rc != 0, "")): the path is taken as not added by wt/a, closing_ref returns None, and the caller uses the
merging branch as the closer, so check_refusal runs against the wrong branch. Expected: a refusal naming the branch whose
diff git could not read, as the rev-list case now does one line below.
fix_hint: rc, added = relay_git.git(...diff...); if rc != 0: raise Refused("cannot list the files %s adds (%s)" % (name, tip)).
pass_cases: - diff fails (mock rc 128, ""): Refused naming wt/a.
- diff succeeds without the path: wt/a skipped, closing_ref returns None (as today).
- diff succeeds with the path, rev-list fails: Refused naming wt/a (the new test, unchanged).
reason: tests/test_merge_hook.py:74 test_a_diff_git_cannot_run_is_a_refusal_naming_the_branch passes; the skip case at line 81 passes.
findings.summary: closing_ref still ignores the exit code of its git diff: a failed diff silently drops that branch from the candidates
